day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight AC arrives at 14:00. Travel from Calgary International Airport to Banff (~1.5 hours by Banff Airporter shuttle, ~$60 CAD one-way). Settle into Banff Mountain Lodge and get oriented.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore downtown Banff on foot. Walk along Banff Avenue, visit the free Cascade Gardens and grounds of the Banff Administration Building, and stroll down to the Bow River pedestrian bridge for stunning mountain views. Pick up a Parks Canada Discovery Pass at the Banff Visitor Centre (~$145 CAD/person for an annual pass — worth it over 6 days to save on park fees).
day_by_day.evening: Easy walk up to the free Bow River Falls viewpoint (15-minute walk from downtown) to watch the golden-hour light on the Rockies. A perfect low-key first evening after travel.

meals.breakfast: Eat at the airport or grab snacks on the shuttle — no breakfast scheduled in Banff.
meals.lunch: Grab a quick and affordable bite at Subway or Nourish Bistro on Banff Avenue upon arrival (~$12–15 CAD).
meals.dinner: Eat at The Maple Leaf Pub & Grill's bar menu or grab a budget-friendly poutine and burger at Banff Ave Brewing Co. (bar snacks ~$15–20 CAD). Alternatively, pick up groceries at Nesters Market on Marten Street to save money for the week.

day_by_day.notes: Priority on Day 1: buy your Parks Canada Discovery Pass — it covers park entry fees and saves money across all days. Nesters Market grocery run is highly recommended for budget travelers to stock up on breakfast items, trail snacks, and lunch supplies for hikes.

day_by_day.morning: Johnston Canyon Waterfall Hike — Depart by 7:30 AM to beat the crowds. Take the Roam Transit Bus #8X from downtown Banff to Johnston Canyon (~$6 CAD round-trip). Follow the famous canyon catwalk trail through the dramatic limestone gorge to the Lower Falls (1.1 km one-way) and Upper Falls (2.7 km one-way). The cool canyon air makes this a perfect morning hike. Allow 2.5–3 hours total.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Banff by midday. After lunch, visit the free Banff Park Museum National Historic Site on Banff Avenue (a charming Victorian-era natural history museum, free with Parks Pass). Then relax at Central Park along the Bow River — bring a book or simply enjoy the mountain scenery.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset walk or easy cycle along the Fenland Trail loop (2 km, flat, free) near the train station — a peaceful forested trail great for wildlife spotting (beavers, deer). Return to lodge for a budget home-cooked dinner.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered breakfast at the lodge using groceries from Nesters Market — oatmeal, fruit, and coffee (~$3–5 CAD).
meals.lunch: Pack a trail lunch from your grocery supplies — sandwiches, trail mix, fruit, and a reusable water bottle filled at the lodge (~$4–6 CAD).
meals.dinner: Cook a simple pasta or rice dish at the lodge, or grab a budget wrap from Tooloulou's on Bear Street (~$14–16 CAD). Check for daily specials.

day_by_day.notes: Start early at Johnston Canyon — by 9 AM it gets very busy, especially in July. Wear layers as the canyon is noticeably cooler than open trails. Roam Transit is a great budget-friendly way to reach trailheads without renting a car.

day_by_day.morning: Moraine Lake — Valley of the Ten Peaks Trek. This is the crown jewel of the trip! Depart very early — take the Parks Canada Moraine Lake Connector shuttle from Lake Louise (book in advance at reservation.pc.gc.ca, ~$20 CAD round-trip). Arrive by 7:00–7:30 AM. Hike the Rockpile Trail (short, 300 m) for the iconic panoramic view of Moraine Lake and the Ten Peaks, then continue along the Lakeshore Trail (3.4 km round-trip, easy) for stunning close-up lake and mountain reflections. Allow 3–4 hours at the lake.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return shuttle to Lake Louise village. Walk around Lake Louise itself (free with Parks Pass) — the 4.4 km lakeshore loop is flat and spectacular. The turquoise water surrounded by Victoria Glacier is breathtaking. Grab a rest on the lakeshore benches.
day_by_day.evening: Take the Roam Transit Bus #8S back to Banff (~$6 CAD). Freshen up at the lodge. Treat yourself to a slightly nicer budget dinner to celebrate a spectacular day.

meals.breakfast: Early self-catered breakfast at the lodge before 6 AM departure — energy bars, banana, instant coffee (~$3 CAD).
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten at Moraine Lake lakeshore — sandwiches, nuts, fruit, chocolate (~$5 CAD). There is a café at Moraine Lake Lodge but it is expensive.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Bear Street Tavern — great wood-fired pizzas at reasonable prices (~$18–22 CAD per person). A well-earned treat after a big hiking day.

day_by_day.notes: CRITICAL: Moraine Lake road is closed to private vehicles in 2027 — shuttle reservation is mandatory. Book the Parks Canada shuttle weeks in advance as spots sell out. Bring layers as mornings at Moraine Lake (elevation 1,885 m) can be chilly even in July. Carry bear spray (rentable in Banff, ~$10/day).

day_by_day.morning: Icefields Parkway Self-Drive & Peyto Lake Viewpoint. Rent a car for the day (~$60–80 CAD budget rental from Enterprise or Hertz in Banff — split costs if traveling with others). Depart by 8:00 AM northbound on Highway 93 (Icefields Parkway). First major stop: Bow Lake viewpoint (free, stunning turquoise glacial lake). Continue to Peyto Lake Viewpoint — hike the short but steep Bow Summit Trail (1.6 km round-trip, 100 m elevation gain) to reach one of the most spectacular panoramic views in the Rockies — a wolf-shaped turquoise lake surrounded by peaks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue north on the Parkway to the Columbia Icefield area. Walk the free viewpoint at the toe of the Athabasca Glacier (do not walk on the glacier without a guide). Enjoy the dramatic scale of the icefield. Begin the scenic return drive south, stopping at Sunwapta Falls (short 0.5 km walk, free) and Athabasca Falls (1 km loop, free) — both spectacular canyon waterfalls.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Banff by 6:00–7:00 PM. Return rental car. Relax at the lodge. Optional: soak tired legs with a short walk to the Bow River.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered early breakfast at lodge before departure (~$3–5 CAD).
meals.lunch: Packed picnic lunch eaten at Peyto Lake or Bow Lake — this is key for budget savings as there are very few affordable food options along the Parkway (~$5–7 CAD packed).
meals.dinner: Budget dinner at Banff's Safeway deli counter or pick up a rotisserie chicken and sides (~$15–18 CAD for a filling meal). Alternatively, Maclab Bistro at the lodge if it has affordable options.

day_by_day.notes: The Icefields Parkway is 230 km one-way to Jasper — this itinerary covers the southern highlights (roughly 140 km north of Banff to Columbia Icefield and back). Gas up in Banff before leaving as fuel is expensive along the Parkway. Carry plenty of water and snacks. Cell service is limited along the entire route.

day_by_day.morning: Sulphur Mountain Hike (budget alternative to the gondola). Instead of paying ~$65 CAD for the gondola, hike up the Sulphur Mountain Trail (5.5 km one-way, 655 m elevation gain, ~2–2.5 hours up). The trail is well-marked and rewarding. At the summit (2,281 m), enjoy 360-degree panoramic views of six mountain ranges, the Bow Valley, and Banff townsite. Walk the free boardwalk to the historic Sanson's Peak Meteorological Station.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the gondola DOWN only (~$25–30 CAD, much cheaper than round-trip) to save your legs for the afternoon. Back in town, visit the free Cave and Basin National Historic Site grounds (the birthplace of Canada's national parks system) and walk the Discovery Trail (1 km loop) through the warm sulfur springs wetlands — great for birdwatching.
day_by_day.evening: Treat yourself to the Banff Upper Hot Springs (~$16.50 CAD adult) — a perfect reward for a big hiking week. Soak in the natural mineral hot springs pool with mountain views. Return to lodge for a relaxed final full evening.

meals.breakfast: Hearty self-catered breakfast before the big hike — oatmeal with peanut butter, banana, coffee (~$4 CAD).
meals.lunch: Pack lunch to eat at the Sulphur Mountain summit — enjoy the views while eating! (~$5 CAD packed).
meals.dinner: Splurge slightly on your second-to-last night — try a shared appetizer and main at Coyotes Southwestern Grill or grab a hearty meal at Eddie Burger + Bar (~$18–22 CAD). Well deserved!

day_by_day.notes: The Sulphur Mountain hike is one of the best free activities in Banff — save ~$40 CAD vs. the round-trip gondola. Start by 8:00 AM to avoid afternoon heat and crowds at the summit. Bring sunscreen and a wind layer for the exposed summit boardwalk. Hot Springs reservation recommended on weekends in July — book online at hotsprings.ca.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — Vermilion Lakes Sunrise Walk. Wake up early for a magical free experience: walk or rent a bike to Vermilion Lakes Drive (5 minutes from downtown). The three lakes offer iconic reflections of Mount Rundle at dawn. Excellent wildlife viewing (elk, herons, ospreys, beavers). Pack up luggage and check out of Banff Mountain Lodge.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure flight time: if time allows, do a short final hike on the Tunnel Mountain Trail (2.3 km one-way, 260 m gain, ~1.5 hours return) — a classic beginner Banff hike with great town and valley views, right next to the lodge. Begin travel back to Calgary for departure (book Banff Airporter shuttle in advance, ~$60 CAD).
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Calgary International Airport. Reflect on an incredible 6-day Banff adventure!

meals.breakfast: Final self-catered breakfast using up remaining groceries from Nesters Market (~$3–5 CAD). Or treat yourself to coffee and a pastry at Whitebark Café on Bear Street (~$8–10 CAD) as a farewell.
meals.lunch: Grab a packed lunch or a quick wrap from a Banff Avenue deli before boarding the shuttle (~$10–14 CAD).
meals.dinner: Airport dining in Calgary or bring snacks for the flight.

day_by_day.notes: Book the Banff Airporter return shuttle to Calgary at least a day in advance — confirm pickup location and time based on your flight. Allow at least 3 hours from Banff to airport check-in (1.5 hr drive + buffer). Leave the national park cleaner than you found it — pack out all waste from trails. Total estimated budget for 6 days (excluding flights and accommodation): ~$400–550 CAD per person, including Parks Pass, transit, one car rental day, meals, and activities.

day_by_day.morning: No morning activities — flight arrives at 14:00. Travel from Calgary Airport to Banff (~1.5 hrs). Check in to Banff Mountain Lodge upon arrival.
day_by_day.afternoon: Settle into the lodge, freshen up, then take a leisurely stroll along the Bow River Trail in downtown Banff. Explore Banff Avenue shops and pick up any hiking supplies needed for the week. Visit the Banff Visitor Centre to orient yourself with the park.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed first evening in Banff. Walk up to the Bow River Bridge viewpoint at dusk for a gentle introduction to the mountain scenery.

meals.breakfast: Grab something at the airport or on the road — Tim Hortons or airport café.
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite en route or at a Canmore café (The Communitea Café is a great mid-range stop on the way).
meals.dinner: Dinner at The Bison Restaurant & Terrace in downtown Banff — mid-range, locally sourced Canadian cuisine with a warm atmosphere. Budget ~CAD $35–50/person.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light — jet lag and travel fatigue are real. Confirm reservations for Moraine Lake shuttle if needed (book in advance as spots fill quickly). Pick up a Parks Canada day pass or confirm your annual pass.

day_by_day.morning: Early start (depart hotel by 7:00 AM) for the Moraine Lake Valley of the Ten Peaks Trek. Take the Parks Canada shuttle from the Banff Gondola/Lake Louise shuttle hub to Moraine Lake (private vehicles restricted). Hike the Rockpile Trail for iconic panoramic views, then continue along the Lakeshore Trail. Allow 3–4 hours total for both trails.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the hike, enjoy lunch near Moraine Lake, then return via shuttle to Lake Louise village. Spend the afternoon exploring the Lake Louise shoreline and the iconic Chateau Lake Louise grounds. Optional: rent a canoe on Lake Louise (~CAD $155/hour for a canoe) for a memorable paddle.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Banff by 6:00 PM. Rest and freshen up before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the lodge or grab a packed breakfast/granola bars for the trail.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on the trail at Moraine Lake — prepare the night before or grab items from Banff's Nesters Market grocery store.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Tooloulou's in Banff — casual Cajun-inspired comfort food, great value, mid-range pricing (~CAD $20–30/person).

day_by_day.notes: Moraine Lake Road is closed to private vehicles — book the Parks Canada shuttle well in advance at reservation.pc.gc.ca. Wear layers; mornings at Moraine Lake can be cool even in July. Bring bear spray (rentable in Banff). Start as early as possible to beat crowds.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day experience: Lake Louise Hike & Canoe. Depart hotel by 8:00 AM and head to Lake Louise. Begin the Plain of Six Glaciers Trail — a stunning 14 km return hike with ~365 m elevation gain, passing glacial moraines and offering jaw-dropping views of Victoria Glacier. The historic Plain of Six Glaciers Teahouse (open seasonally) makes a perfect turnaround point for refreshments.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend back to Lake Louise and reward yourself with a canoe rental on the lake (~CAD $155/hour). Paddle with the backdrop of the Victoria Glacier and the Fairmont Chateau Lake Louise. Explore the lakeshore and interpretive signs before heading back.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back to Banff (~45 min). Relax at the lodge before a well-earned dinner.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the lodge or a quick stop at Lake Louise Village's Laggan's Mountain Bakery — excellent pastries and coffee at a reasonable price.
meals.lunch: The Plain of Six Glaciers Teahouse on the trail (cash only, seasonal) — soups, sandwiches, and baked goods. A unique experience worth the hike. Budget ~CAD $15–20.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Coyotes Southwestern Grill in Banff — fresh, flavourful Southwestern cuisine, great vegetarian options, mid-range (~CAD $25–40/person).

day_by_day.notes: The Plain of Six Glaciers trail is moderately strenuous — wear sturdy hiking boots and bring trekking poles if available. The Teahouse is cash only and closes in bad weather. Book canoe rentals at the Fairmont boathouse early in the day to secure your time slot.

day_by_day.morning: Drive the legendary Icefields Parkway (Highway 93) — one of the world's most scenic roads. Depart Banff by 8:30 AM. Head north, stopping at Bow Lake (stunning turquoise glacial lake with easy shoreline walk), then continue to the Peyto Lake Viewpoint. The short hike up to the Bow Summit lookout (~1 km each way) rewards with one of the most spectacular lake views in the Rockies — Peyto Lake's vivid blue-green waters surrounded by peaks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue north to the Columbia Icefield area (optional stop at the Athabasca Glacier viewpoint — free to view from the road). Begin the return drive south along the Parkway, stopping at Mistaya Canyon for a short 1 km walk to a dramatic limestone gorge. Arrive back in Banff by 5:00–6:00 PM.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxing evening in downtown Banff. Browse the shops or visit the Whyte Museum of the Canadian Rockies for a cultural wind-down.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the lodge before departure.
meals.lunch: Packed picnic lunch enjoyed at Bow Lake — one of the most scenic picnic spots in the Rockies. Pick up supplies from Nesters Market the evening before.
meals.dinner: Dinner at The Bear Street Tavern in Banff — wood-fired pizza and craft beer in a cozy setting, excellent mid-range value (~CAD $20–35/person).

day_by_day.notes: Fill up on gas in Banff before departing — fuel is limited and expensive along the Parkway. The Icefields Parkway is ~230 km one-way to Jasper; this itinerary covers the southern highlights without going all the way to Jasper. Bring a camera — wildlife sightings (elk, bears, mountain goats) are common. Check Parks Canada road reports before departure.

day_by_day.morning: Johnston Canyon Waterfall Hike. Depart hotel by 9:00 AM and drive ~25 min west on the Trans-Canada to Johnston Canyon. Follow the iconic canyon catwalk trail — a dramatic suspended walkway bolted into limestone canyon walls — to the Lower Falls (1.1 km one-way) and Upper Falls (2.7 km one-way). The Upper Falls cascade 30 metres and are well worth the extra distance. Optional extension to the Inkpots (5.8 km one-way) — seven cold mineral springs in an open meadow with mountain views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Banff by early afternoon. Take the Sulphur Mountain Gondola ride up to 2,281 metres for panoramic 360-degree views of six mountain ranges and the Bow Valley. Walk the Summit Boardwalk (1 km) along the ridge to Sanson's Peak meteorological station. Allow 2–3 hours total.
day_by_day.evening: Final full evening in Banff. Treat yourself to a slightly elevated dinner to celebrate the trip.

meals.lunch: Lunch at the Johnston Canyon Resort café/restaurant near the trailhead — casual dining with sandwiches and soups (~CAD $15–25).
meals.dinner: Dinner at Eden Restaurant at the Rimrock Resort Hotel — a splurge-worthy fine dining experience with panoramic mountain views. A special mid-range splurge (~CAD $60–90/person) to celebrate the trip. Alternatively, stay mid-range at Saltlik Steakhouse on Banff Avenue (~CAD $40–60/person).

day_by_day.notes: Johnston Canyon can be busy on weekends — arrive before 9:30 AM to secure parking. The catwalk can be slippery; wear grippy hiking shoes. The Banff Gondola costs ~CAD $65/adult — book online in advance for a small discount. Sunset from the gondola summit is spectacular if timing allows.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Banff. Take a peaceful early walk along the Vermilion Lakes Drive — a flat, easy 5 km trail with stunning reflections of Mount Rundle on the lakes and frequent wildlife sightings (elk, beavers, herons). A perfect, gentle farewell to the Rockies.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of Banff Mountain Lodge (standard check-out 11:00 AM — store luggage if needed). Grab a final stroll through downtown Banff for any last-minute souvenirs. Drive back to Calgary Airport (~1.5 hrs), allowing ample time for check-in and security.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Calgary. Carry the memories of the Rockies home.

meals.breakfast: Farewell breakfast at Whitebark Café in Banff — beloved local café with excellent coffee, eggs, and baked goods. A Banff institution (~CAD $15–20).
meals.lunch: Light lunch at Nourish Bistro in Banff before departure — creative, plant-forward menu in a cozy setting (~CAD $18–28). Or grab road snacks from Nesters Market for the drive.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Calgary Airport or en route if flight timing allows.

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5 hours before your flight departure time to account for the drive and airport security. Return any rented gear (bear spray, trekking poles) before leaving Banff. Keep your Parks Canada pass handy until you exit the park boundary.

day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury transfer from Calgary Airport to Banff (~1.5 hrs). Check in to Banff Mountain Lodge, unpack, and take a leisurely self-guided stroll along the Bow River Promenade in downtown Banff to acclimate to the mountain air and scenery.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on the hotel terrace or rooftop lounge overlooking the Banff townsite and surrounding peaks. Enjoy a welcome dinner at The Maple Leaf Restaurant – a Banff institution renowned for its elevated Canadian cuisine featuring Alberta beef, wild game, and Pacific seafood in a warm, lodge-inspired setting.

meals.lunch: Grab a premium charcuterie box or artisan sandwich at Whitebark Café in the Fairmont Banff Springs area upon arrival, or enjoy light bites in the hotel lounge upon check-in.
meals.dinner: The Maple Leaf Restaurant, Banff – signature Alberta bison tenderloin or wild Pacific salmon, paired with a curated Canadian wine selection. Reserve ahead for a window table.

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange a private luxury vehicle transfer from Calgary Airport (e.g., Banff Airporter Executive or a private car service) for a seamless arrival experience. Confirm hotel check-in time is aligned with your 14:00 arrival. Light evening walk in Banff townsite is ideal for gentle acclimatization to altitude (~1,383 m).

day_by_day.morning: Moraine Lake Valley of the Ten Peaks Trek – Depart early (6:00–6:30 AM) by private vehicle or pre-booked Parks Canada shuttle to beat the mandatory reservation window. Hike the Rockpile Trail for the iconic Valley of the Ten Peaks panorama, then continue along the Lakeshore Trail (5.8 km round trip) skirting the impossibly turquoise glacial waters. Option to add a guided interpretation walk with a private naturalist guide for an elevated experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the morning trek, return to Lake Louise Village (~45 min drive). Enjoy a gourmet lakeside lunch at the Fairmont Chateau Lake Louise's Lakeview Lounge. Spend the afternoon on the Lake Louise Hike & Canoe experience – paddle a premium canoe across the iconic jade waters of Lake Louise beneath the Victoria Glacier, then hike a portion of the Plain of Six Glaciers Trail (up to the historic teahouse, ~10.8 km return) for breathtaking glacier and mountain views.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Banff Mountain Lodge by private transfer. Indulge in a restorative mountain spa treatment (hot stone massage or alpine aromatherapy) at the hotel or a nearby luxury spa. Dinner at Eden Restaurant at the Rimrock Resort Hotel – Banff's most acclaimed fine dining destination, offering a six-course tasting menu with locally foraged ingredients and an award-winning wine cellar.

meals.breakfast: Early gourmet breakfast at Banff Mountain Lodge – smoked salmon eggs Benedict or a full Canadian spread – before the 6:00 AM departure.
meals.lunch: Lakeview Lounge, Fairmont Chateau Lake Louise – Alberta beef burger or fresh-caught trout with Lake Louise as your backdrop.
meals.dinner: Eden Restaurant, Rimrock Resort Hotel – six-course chef's tasting menu with optional wine pairing. Reservations essential; book weeks in advance.

Bring layers as temperatures at Moraine Lake can be 5–8°C cooler than Banff townsite even in July. Canoe rentals at Lake Louise are available through the Fairmont boathouse – premium guided options available.

day_by_day.morning: Sulphur Mountain Gondola & Summit Boardwalk – Board the Banff Gondola (just minutes from downtown Banff) for the 8-minute ride to the 2,281-metre summit of Sulphur Mountain. Walk the 1-km Summit Boardwalk connecting two peaks with sweeping 360° panoramas of six mountain ranges, the Bow Valley, and the Banff townsite far below. Visit the restored Sanson's Peak Meteorological Station for historical context. Ideal photo opportunities in the clear morning light.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend via gondola and head to the Banff Upper Hot Springs for a premium soak in the historic natural mineral pools with mountain views – a restorative luxury after the summit experience. Afterward, explore the boutique galleries and artisan shops of Banff Avenue, or visit the Whyte Museum of the Canadian Rockies for curated insights into mountain culture and history.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset hike or guided e-bike tour along the Tunnel Mountain Trail (2.7 km loop) for golden-hour views over the Bow Valley – a gentle, rewarding evening activity. Dinner at Saltlik Steakhouse – Banff's premier steakhouse featuring prime-cut AAA Alberta beef, dry-aged in-house, with an extensive bourbon and whisky selection.

meals.breakfast: Juniper Bistro at The Juniper Hotel – seasonal farm-to-table breakfast with panoramic Banff valley views; excellent eggs, fresh pastries, and locally sourced meats.
meals.lunch: Sky Bistro at the top of the Banff Gondola – elevated Canadian cuisine at 2,281 metres; smoked Alberta bison flatbread or wild mushroom risotto with unbeatable views.
meals.dinner: Saltlik Steakhouse, Banff Avenue – prime 45-day dry-aged ribeye or tomahawk steak with truffle fries and a bottle from their acclaimed wine cellar.

day_by_day.notes: The Banff Gondola opens at 8:00 AM in summer – arriving early avoids crowds and offers the best morning light for photography. The Banff Upper Hot Springs are open daily; private changing facilities and towel rentals available. Book the gondola and Sky Bistro online in advance to secure preferred time slots.

day_by_day.morning: Johnston Canyon Waterfall Hike – Drive ~25 minutes west of Banff to Johnston Canyon. Walk the dramatic suspended catwalk trail bolted into the limestone canyon walls to the Lower Falls (1.1 km) and Upper Falls (2.7 km from trailhead). For the adventurous, continue to the Ink Pots – seven vivid cold-water springs in a meadow above the canyon (5.8 km one way). Hire a private interpretive guide for an enriched natural history experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Banff for a leisurely afternoon. Enjoy a private fly-fishing excursion on the Bow River with a licensed guide – one of Canada's premier trout fisheries, offering a quintessential Rocky Mountain luxury experience. Alternatively, book a private helicopter sightseeing tour over the Banff backcountry and glaciers for an unforgettable aerial perspective of the Canadian Rockies.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening in Banff townsite. Pre-dinner drinks at the Bear Street Tavern's craft cocktail bar, then a refined dinner at 1888 Chop House inside the Fairmont Banff Springs Hotel – a grand historic dining room featuring prime Alberta cuts, fresh seafood towers, and an exceptional sommelier-curated wine list in a castle-like atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast at Banff Mountain Lodge – avocado toast with smoked trout, fresh-pressed juices, and artisan coffee to fuel the morning hike.
meals.lunch: Packed gourmet picnic lunch prepared by the hotel (request in advance) – enjoyed at the Ink Pots meadow or along the canyon trail; smoked salmon wraps, artisan cheese, fruit, and sparkling water.
meals.dinner: 1888 Chop House, Fairmont Banff Springs Hotel – prime Alberta beef tenderloin or whole roasted rack of lamb, with a classic Canadian cheese board to finish. Dress smart-casual.

day_by_day.notes: Johnston Canyon is one of Banff's most popular trails – arriving before 8:00 AM on a Saturday is strongly recommended to avoid crowds. The catwalk can be slippery; wear hiking footwear with grip. Fly-fishing and helicopter tours must be booked in advance through licensed Banff operators (e.g., Banff Fishing Unlimited or Alpine Helicopters).

day_by_day.morning: Icefields Parkway Self-Drive & Peyto Lake Viewpoint – Depart Banff at 7:00 AM in a premium rental vehicle (or private chauffeured SUV) for the legendary Icefields Parkway (Highway 93 North). Stop at Bow Lake (stunning turquoise glacial lake) and hike the short trail to the Peyto Lake Viewpoint (~40-min return) for the iconic wolf-head-shaped turquoise lake panorama – arguably the most spectacular viewpoint in the Canadian Rockies. Continue north to the Columbia Icefield area.
day_by_day.afternoon: At the Columbia Icefield, board the Ice Explorer glacier adventure vehicle for a guided tour onto the Athabasca Glacier – walk on 10,000-year-old glacial ice and learn about climate change impacts from expert guides. Visit the Glacier Skywalk, a glass-floored observation platform suspended 280 metres above the Sunwapta Valley. Begin the scenic return drive south along the Parkway, stopping at Mistaya Canyon and Crowfoot Glacier viewpoints.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive back in Banff by early evening. Wind down with a private in-room couple's spa treatment arranged through the hotel – hot stone massage or mountain herb wrap using locally sourced botanicals. Farewell-eve dinner at The Bison Restaurant & Terrace – Banff's beloved farm-to-table gem, celebrating local Rocky Mountain ingredients: bison, elk, wild mushrooms, and Alberta-grown produce on a beautiful outdoor terrace.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at the hotel (continental spread or grab-and-go smoked salmon bagel and coffee) before the 7:00 AM departure.
meals.lunch: Num-Ti-Jah Lodge at Bow Lake – a historic backcountry lodge on the Parkway with a charming dining room; wild mushroom soup and bison chili with Bow Lake views. Alternatively, a gourmet packed lunch from the hotel enjoyed at a scenic Parkway pullout.
meals.dinner: The Bison Restaurant & Terrace, Banff – Alberta bison short rib or wild elk medallions with roasted root vegetables, paired with a local craft beer or British Columbia Pinot Noir on the heated terrace.

day_by_day.notes: The full Icefields Parkway round trip from Banff to Columbia Icefield and back is approximately 430 km – allow a full day. A private chauffeured vehicle (e.g., Pursuit/Brewster luxury tours) is an excellent premium option so you can focus entirely on the scenery. Book Ice Explorer and Glacier Skywalk tickets online in advance. Bring sunscreen, sunglasses, and a warm layer – temperatures on the icefield can be significantly colder.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning hike – Tunnel Mountain Summit Trail (4.8 km return, ~1.5 hrs) departing from near the hotel for a gentle but rewarding farewell to Banff's mountains, with sweeping views of the Bow Valley, Hoodoos, and surrounding peaks in the clear morning light. A perfect, unhurried send-off hike accessible directly from the townsite. Return to hotel for a leisurely checkout breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Late checkout (arrange with hotel for 12:00–13:00). Spend remaining time browsing Banff's finest boutiques on Bear Street for premium Canadian souvenirs – locally made jewelry, artisan chocolates from Welch's Chocolate Shop, or bespoke Indigenous artwork. Private luxury transfer departs Banff at ~13:30 to Calgary International Airport (~1.5 hrs), allowing ample time for check-in and departure.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Calgary International Airport. If flight timing allows, enjoy a final meal at the airport's premium lounge or Sky 360 Restaurant at the Calgary Tower (en route stop) – revolving restaurant with panoramic Calgary skyline views and classic Alberta beef.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely final breakfast at Banff Mountain Lodge – full Canadian spread: eggs your way, smoked Alberta back bacon, fresh-baked pastries, seasonal fruit, and specialty coffee. Savor the mountain views one last time.
meals.lunch: Coyotes Southwestern Grill, Banff – a beloved local favourite for a relaxed final lunch; Southwest-inspired dishes with fresh Rocky Mountain ingredients. Or a quick premium sandwich from a Bear Street deli for the road.
meals.dinner: En route or at Calgary Airport premium lounge / Sky 360 Restaurant at the Calgary Tower (if schedule permits a stop) – Alberta beef tenderloin or a classic Canadian poutine with premium Quebec cheese curds as a final indulgence.

day_by_day.notes: Confirm late checkout with Banff Mountain Lodge at time of booking to avoid rushing on departure day. Private transfer to Calgary Airport should be booked to depart no later than 13:30 for a comfortable arrival with 2–3 hours before international or domestic departure. Ensure all Parks Canada park passes are returned or noted as expired. Tipping guides, drivers, and hotel staff generously is customary at the luxury level.
